title: Louis Armstrong's singing and improvisation
summary: Purnell says Louis sings the way he plays and has fresh ideas; original New Orleans players never play a thing the same way twice.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Alton, do you find that Louis sings about the way he plays?

Yeah, he does sing about the way he plays, you know. He's got a wonderful mind, man. He makes some of the stuff, all the stuff that he does on his trumpet is really new, man. You know, he's got wonderful ideas. He should be an arranger.
Well, I think he probably does that as he goes along all the time. He's busy arranging things from time to time.
Yeah, well... Well, all you fellows do.
I mean, you never play the same thing twice the same way.

Most of the original jazz men from down in New Orleans always play that way, you know. It's hard to explain how these things come from your mind into your fingers or the way you play them, but they all fit in, you know.
